items.text: In adults ventilated in intensive care for more than 48 hours, are diaries written mainly by relatives, compared with staff-written diaries or no diary, associated with fewer post-traumatic stress, anxiety or depression symptoms in patients and relatives 3 to 12 months later?
items.population: Adult intensive care survivors ventilated more than 48 hours and their relatives
items.intervention: Diary written mainly by relatives and read with the patient after discharge
items.comparator: Staff-written diary, mixed diary or no diary
items.outcome: Post-traumatic stress, anxiety and depression symptoms

items.text: How do relatives and survivors describe writing and reading a family-led diary, and what harms or barriers do they report?
items.population: Relatives who kept a diary and survivors who read one
items.intervention: Writing and reading a family-led diary
items.setting: Intensive care units and follow-up clinics

finer: Feasible within 40 hours with library support; interesting to nursing, medicine and the follow-up clinic; novel only for the unit; ethical as a literature review; relevant because a guideline depends on it.
summary: One effects question and one experience question for the review.
